paper.title: Benchmarking mutation effect prediction algorithms using functionally validated cancer-related missense mutations
paper.citation: Martelotto LG, Ng CKY, De Filippo MR, Zhang Y, Piscuoglio S, Lim RS, Shen R, Norton L, Reis-Filho JS, Weigelt B. Benchmarking mutation effect prediction algorithms using functionally validated cancer-related missense mutations. Genome Biology 15:484 (2014)

calls.what: A call the predictor did not make (CanDrA 'No-call', FATHMM (missense) 'No weights', Mutation Assessor N/A) is left out of that predictor's performance counts. The paper calls the no-call 'equivocal' without saying how it enters the statistics; we tried leaving it out, counting it as neutral and counting it as non-neutral.
calls.sensitivity: Left out, every point value of Tables 3 and 4 comes back. Counted as neutral, CanDrA (lung) accuracy on the 989 SNVs is 89.28% and counted as non-neutral 90.19%, against the printed 91.28%.

bootstrap.what: 95% intervals are percentile intervals of 1,000 resamples of the labelled SNVs with replacement, not stratified by label (the paper gives neither the interval method nor the stratification), with fixed seeds.
bootstrap.sensitivity: Chosen by comparing interval widths with Table 3: resampling within each label narrows the intervals that depend on the number of neutral SNVs (CHASM (breast) NPV about 51.9-62.7% against the printed 50.23-64.58%; unstratified 50.2-64.2%).

bootstrap.what: Tolerance of an interval end: half a printed unit plus 3 x sqrt(2) standard deviations of that end over 20 repeat bootstraps with other seeds (the paper's seeds are unknown).

kappa.what: In Cohen's kappa and the clustering, a missing call is a third category ('equivocal'), and the kappa interval is kappa +/- 1.96 SE0, SE0 being the standard error under kappa = 0 (Fleiss, Cohen and Everitt 1969), capped at 1.
kappa.sensitivity: Dropping the pairs with a missing call instead gives CHASM (breast) / CanDrA (lung) kappa 0.8453 against the printed 0.7537. With z = 1.959964 instead of 1.96, 56 of the 2,880 printed kappa values and interval ends of Additional files 3, 5, 11 and 13 miss by one unit in the fourth significant digit.

low.what: The low-confidence score intervals include their end points, and a call the predictor did not make (FATHMM (missense) 'No weights', Mutation Assessor N/A) is of low confidence.
low.sensitivity: These give all 44 counts of Additional file 9. With open intervals 28 of the 44 differ; without the missing calls as low confidence 14 differ.

splits.what: Combinations: 1,000 random splits of the labelled SNVs into subset 1 (round(2/3 n) SNVs drawn without replacement, not stratified) and subset 2; mean and 2.5/97.5 percentiles over the splits; a missing call does not count as non-neutral; fixed seeds (1 and, for the second run, 2).

Tolerance of a mean or interval end over the splits: half a printed unit plus 3 times the RMS difference between our two runs over all 11,253 combinations (the paper's splits are unknown). For Additional files 17 and 18, the mean's own standard error (its spread over the splits / sqrt(1,000), times sqrt(2)).

drawing.what: Values read from the vector drawing of the PMC PDF: each axis is calibrated from its own tick marks and printed tick labels (least squares, residual below 1e-4 of the axis unit); a bar of height zero has no drawing and reads as the axis base.
drawing.sensitivity: The tolerance (0.0005 of the 0-1 axes, 0.002 of the 0-4 composite axes) is about four times the reading precision (PDF coordinates to 0.01 pt on axes of about 70 pt).

fig1.what: Fig. 1: the predictor order and the dendrograms' clades transcribed by eye (published/fig1_reading.json); each kappa cell's colour matched to the nearest colour of the key; each row's shares of non-neutral, neutral and no call found by unmixing the row's mean colour into the three key colours; join heights read from the vector dendrogram relative to the root.
fig1.sensitivity: Shares agree within 0.0065 at most; at a tolerance of 0.005 instead of 0.01, 77 of the 90 shares match. The nearest key colour is at most 0.0044 (RGB 0-1) from every cell's colour.

ci_onc.summary: Most of the interval ends outside the tolerance belong to the oncogenes, which have 7 neutral SNVs, so the ends of specificity, NPV and composite jump between a few possible values. Three of them do not move at all across our 20 repeat bootstraps and still miss: CanDrA (melanoma) specificity low end (printed 14.29%, ours 0% in every repeat), CanDrA (lung) NPV low end (11.11%, ours 0% or near it) and CanDrA (lung) accuracy high end (98.15%, ours 98.12%). Tables 3 and 4 do not show this, so the paper's resampling of the oncogene set differed in a way we have not found.

hypotheses.test: 20 repeat bootstraps: the three ends are the same in every repeat.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Resampling all labelled SNVs, no-calls included, and dropping the no-calls afterwards.
hypotheses.test: 1,000 resamples x 20 seeds for CanDrA (melanoma) and CanDrA (lung) on the oncogenes: specificity low end 0% and accuracy high end 98.05-98.13%, as before.

mc_box.summary: The 8 hinges and medians outside the tolerance are those of the combinations of 10 and 11 predictors that need 10 or 11 non-neutral calls; they miss by 0.1 point at most. The tolerance uses the average run-to-run spread of a combination's mean accuracy (0.025 point RMS); these combinations spread more (the one of all 11 has a standard error of 0.036 point, so 3 x sqrt(2) of it is 0.15 point, which holds the 0.097 gap). Our second run moves its mean by 0.028 point.

t4text.summary: CanDrA (melanoma)'s accuracy without COSMIC (Table 4 high end 86.64%) and with it (Table 3 low end 87.02%) almost touch, so whether the drop is significant depends on the resamples: 13 predictors in the paper, 12 in our run. From the paper's own intervals the call comes back, but only {rep_text_table4_8} of our 20 repeat bootstraps give it, so a different seed alone is an unlikely cause; the paper's interval method may differ in a way the other intervals do not show.

combtext.summary: The counts and the best combination's means and intervals come from random splits. Our second run gives {acc_both_run2} combinations above FATHMM (cancer)'s accuracy in both subsets ({acc_sig_run2} significantly) and {comp_both_run2} above CHASM (lung)'s composite ({comp_sig_run2} significantly), against the paper's 1,854 (6) and 1,483 (5). Recomputed from the means and intervals the paper prints in Additional file 17 (arithmetic column), the counts are 1,853 (6) and 1,482 (5): the printed means are rounded, so combinations right at FATHMM (cancer)'s or CHASM (lung)'s value can fall either way. The best combination's values come back from Additional file 21.

cause.summary: Both sentences have n and p swapped: the paper's own Additional file 25, and our run, give a best n of about 2p (p about n/2), capped at all 11 predictors. Our run gives the same optimal p or n as Additional file 25 in all 21 rows; in one row (n = 8) the best combination has SIFT where the file has VEST (af25).

exceptions.field: for n = 1 to 4, the best p is about 2n
exceptions.evidence: Additional file 25 (B) gives p = 1, 1, 2 for n = 2, 3, 4: the best p is about n/2 (n about 2p), as the next sentence's 'n approximately p/2' would say were it also reversed. p <= n everywhere, so p about 2n cannot hold.

exceptions.field: for p = 3 to 11, the best n is about p/2
exceptions.evidence: Additional file 25 (A) gives n = 6, 7, 9, 10 for p = 3 to 6 and n = 11 (all predictors) for p = 7 to 11: the best n is about 2p, capped at 11. n >= p everywhere, so n about p/2 cannot hold.

page.lede: Martelotto and colleagues scored 15 mutation effect predictors, and 11,253 ways of combining them, on 989 cancer mutations whose effect is known. Their statistics code was never shared. We rebuilt it from the paper as the package mutbench and reran it on their own spreadsheet.

page.tables_caption: Every point value came back. The intervals come from random resampling: {table3_ci_match} of 180 and {table4_ci_match} of 180 interval ends are within the spread of our own repeat runs.
page.items_caption: {items} results: {exact} exact, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly agree, {differs} differ, {not_attempted} not attempted. Each verdict is computed from the numbers by check_results.py.

buried: The authors' code. It was never released; the method is rebuilt from the text.

The exact random splits and resamples. Counts of combinations near a cutoff and the order of near ties move with them: 1,854 combinations beat FATHMM (cancer) in both subsets in the paper and in our run, and 6 of them significantly in the paper, 5 in ours.
Two sentences on the optimal n and p have n and p swapped. The paper's own Additional file 25 agrees with our run, not with the sentences.
Additional file 8 leaves out Mutation Assessor's 7 N/A calls; Additional file 9 counts them as low confidence.
Additional file 2 swaps the headers of FATHMM's two training-set columns. We read them by their content.
page.claims_line: The main finding holds: no single predictor is accurate enough, and combining CHASM (breast) with MutationTaster ranks first by accuracy and composite score in both subsets, with an NPV significantly above the best single and meta-predictor, as the paper says. Most claims that do not match move with the random splits or resamples; one significance call does not come back for a reason we have not found; two sentences are the paper's own slip.
page.matched_intro: What our run had to match, and how closely.
matched: As printed, to four significant digits.

Within half a printed unit plus three standard deviations of the difference between two of our runs.
page.closing: Fig. 2 came back the same. The benchmark is a package now.
